answer:
Based on the search results, **Ibn Sina** (known in the West as **Avicenna**, c. 980–1037) is widely considered the most influential philosopher in Islamic history. He was a polymath who wrote extensively across numerous disciplines including philosophy, medicine, astronomy, and mathematics.

According to historical records:
- **~450 works** are believed to have been written by Ibn Sina
- Approximately **240 of these works have survived** to the present day
- Of the surviving works: ~150 focused on philosophy and ~40 on medicine

Among his surviving works were major encyclopedias such as **"Kitāb al-shifāʾ"** (The Book of Healing/The Cure), which covered logic, physics, mathematics, and metaphysics, and **"al-Qanūn fī al-Tibb"** (The Canon of Medicine), a seminal medical text that influenced medical education for centuries.
